title: Multi-Availability Zone VPC design patterns
hook: Production VPC design mirrors Availability Zone boundaries: public and private subnet pairs per AZ, NAT Gateway per AZ, Application Load Balancer spanning AZs, and databases in private subnets with Multi-AZ — one AZ can fail without taking down the entire application.

blocks.text: The standard highly available VPC pattern places an Internet Gateway on the VPC, two or more public subnets (one per AZ) for ALB and NAT Gateway, and matching private subnets for compute and data. Each private subnet in an AZ routes 0.0.0.0/0 to a NAT Gateway in the public subnet of the same AZ. ALB registers targets across AZ private subnets. RDS subnet group spans private subnets; RDS Multi-AZ keeps synchronous standby in another AZ.

entries.plainDefinition: Matched public and private subnets in each Availability Zone.
ALB sends traffic to healthy targets in any enabled AZ.
entries.example: AZ-a outage — ALB serves from AZ-b targets only.

entries.plainDefinition: RDS requirement spanning subnets in at least two AZs.
entries.example: Private subnets in 1a and 1b for Multi-AZ PostgreSQL.

entries.plainDefinition: Partial or full loss of one AZ — design goal is continued service.
entries.example: Lost NAT in 1a affects only 1a private egress if isolated RTs.

blocks.text: This is the VPC diagram interviewers ask you to draw from memory. Single-AZ VPC patterns fail real outages. Cost of three NAT Gateways is cheaper than hours of company-wide egress outage. C# ASP.NET Core on EC2, Node on ECS, or Java on EKS all sit in the same VPC skeleton.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: Draw IGW, per-AZ public (ALB+NAT), per-AZ private (app+DB), per-AZ private RT to local NAT, RDS Multi-AZ, ALB cross-zone enabled.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: VPC /16 CIDR
items.body: Plan three public /24 and three private /24 blocks across AZs.

items.title: Edge tier
items.body: IGW attached; ALB in public subnets; security group allows 443 from internet to ALB only.

items.title: App tier
items.body: EC2/ECS/EKS in private subnets; SG allows traffic from ALB SG only.

items.title: Data tier
items.body: RDS Multi-AZ in private subnet group; no public accessibility.

items.title: Egress tier
items.body: NAT Gateway + EIP in each public subnet; private RT per AZ points to local NAT.

diagram.title: Three-AZ VPC pattern
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  IGW[Internet Gateway]
  subgraph AZa["AZ-a"]
    PubA[Public + NAT + ALB]
    PrivA[Private app]
  end
  subgraph AZb["AZ-b"]
    PubB[Public + NAT + ALB]
    PrivB[Private app]
  end
  subgraph AZc["AZ-c"]
    PubC[Public + NAT + ALB]
    PrivC[Private app]
  end
  Internet((Internet)) --> IGW --> PubA
  IGW --> PubB
  IGW --> PubC
  PubA --> PrivA
  PubB --> PrivB
  PubC --> PrivC
  PrivA --> RDS[(RDS Multi-AZ)]
  PrivB --> RDS
  PrivC --> RDS

snippet.label: Multi-AZ ALB and target group
snippet.code:
ApplicationLoadBalancer:
  Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::LoadBalancer
  Properties:
    Scheme: internet-facing
    Subnets:
      - !Ref PublicSubnetA
      - !Ref PublicSubnetB
      - !Ref PublicSubnetC
    SecurityGroups:
      - !Ref AlbSecurityGroup
AppTargetGroup:
  Type: AWS::ElasticLoadBalancingV2::TargetGroup
  Properties:
    Port: 8080
    Protocol: HTTP
    VpcId: !Ref AppVpc
    TargetType: instance
    HealthCheckPath: /health
snippet.explanation: ALB requires minimum two subnets in two AZs. Targets register from private subnets across AZs.

snippet.label: RDS Multi-AZ in private subnet group
snippet.code:
DbSubnetGroup:
  Type: AWS::RDS::DBSubnetGroup
  Properties:
    SubnetIds:
      - !Ref PrivateSubnetA
      - !Ref PrivateSubnetB
      - !Ref PrivateSubnetC
ProdDatabase:
  Type: AWS::RDS::DBInstance
  Properties:
    Engine: postgres
    MultiAZ: true
    DBSubnetGroupName: !Ref DbSubnetGroup
    PubliclyAccessible: false
snippet.explanation: MultiAZ true creates synchronous standby in another AZ. PubliclyAccessible false keeps database off internet path.

snippet.label: Validate subnet AZ spread
snippet.explanation: Confirm public and private subnets exist in each AZ before declaring HA complete.

sections.heading: Compare with on-premises and C# backends

blocks.title: Multi-AZ VPC vs dual-site on-prem
rows: Survive one AZ / data center loss in Region
Same Docker image to ECS tasks in each AZ
Same MSI deploy to both halls

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Single NAT shared across AZs. ALB in one public subnet only (needs two AZ minimum). RDS in one private subnet single-AZ. App SG allowing 0.0.0.0/0 instead of ALB SG reference. Forgetting VPC endpoints and overloading NAT.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: GameDay AZ failure simulation — disable one AZ subnet route or use fault injection; verify ALB healthy target count and RDS failover time. CloudWatch alarms on NAT per AZ. Cost optimization: reduce to two AZs if third AZ adds little benefit for small workloads — but never one AZ for prod. EKS: pods spread with topologySpreadConstraints; Fargate: platform version across AZ subnets. Flow logs per tier prove traffic never hits IGW from database subnets.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: Lose one AZ capacity slice on impairment
Not production — say so explicitly in interview
Writer in one AZ — readers in others for scale

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Whiteboard with one public subnet, one private subnet, one NAT, RDS public. Strong answer: labeled AZ columns, ALB only public entry, SG references not CIDRs, Multi-AZ RDS, NAT per AZ.

interviewTakeaways: Production VPC = public + private subnet pair per AZ, NAT per AZ, ALB across public subnets, RDS Multi-AZ in private subnet group.
Route tables must isolate NAT failure to the affected AZ only.
Application security groups reference ALB security group — not open internet on app ports.
60s: Draw three AZ columns. IGW top. ALB+NAT public each AZ. App private. RDS Multi-AZ private. NAT per AZ RT.
Follow-up: when is two AZ enough versus three?
commonPitfalls: Single NAT diagram gets you rejected immediately in senior VPC interviews.
Strong answer: complete labeled multi-AZ diagram with SG relationships stated aloud.
ALB with one subnet — CloudFormation deploy failure or no HA.
Multi-AZ RDS but app tier single-AZ — DB fails over while all app capacity was in dead AZ.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Fargate service desiredCount 3 across three AZ subnets — same as running three Node PM2 clusters in three on-prem halls behind a load balancer.
When AZ-a impaired, ALB drains unhealthy targets — TypeScript API pods in AZ-b absorb load like C# web farm losing one hall without DNS change.
